---
title: "RevealJS Fragmention"
subtitle: "Reveal a whole list item, marker and all."
description: "What the fragmention extension is for, how to enable it, and why a bare fragment on a list leaves the bullets behind."
authors:
  - name: "Mickaël CANOUIL, _Ph.D._"
    orcid: "0000-0002-3396-4549"
    url: "https://mickael.canouil.fr"
---

Putting a RevealJS fragment on a list item marks the text, not the item, so the bullets and numbers all appear at once while the words arrive one by one.
The list looks broken for as long as it takes to fill in.

`fragmention` moves the fragment up to the item.
Write an empty marker span at the start and its classes and attributes are hoisted onto the `<li>`, so the marker arrives with its text.

## Installation

```bash
quarto add {{< var extension.reference >}}
```

This will install the extension under the `_extensions` subdirectory.
If you are using version control, you will want to check in this directory.

Or install it from your editor with [Quarto Wizard](https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-wizard):

::: {.btn-group role="group" aria-label="Quarto Wizard installer options"}

## Quick start

```yaml
filters:
  - fragmention
```

Then start each item with an empty `.fragment` span:

```markdown
- []{.fragment fragment-index="1"} First item.
- []{.fragment fragment-index="2"} Second item.
- A normal item, with no fragment.
```

The span is removed and its classes and attributes land on the item, so RevealJS controls the whole thing.
